Counts are Female 31 and Male 49. The design matrix is `[1, Age, BMI, GenderMale]`.

## Fitted combined model

```r
model_combined <- glm(
  Response ~ Age + BMI + Gender,
  data = dataset,
  family = binomial
)
```

The fitted linear predictor is:

```text
logit[P(Response=1)]
  = beta_0
  + beta_Age × Age
  + beta_BMI × BMI
  + beta_Male × I(Gender=Male)
```

| term | Estimate | Std. Error |
|---|---:|---:|
| `(Intercept)` | 1.5312885111 | 2.7755318647 |
| Age | -0.0795084690 | 0.0262977303 |
| BMI | 0.1621226647 | 0.1088272869 |
| GenderMale | -0.6131991352 | 0.5471262859 |

The combined model has residual deviance `97.1572197990` and AIC `105.1572197990`.

Holding BMI and gender fixed,

```text
eta(age + 1) - eta(age) = beta_Age
```

The corresponding one-year odds multiplier is `exp(beta_Age)=0.9235701982`. A log-odds change, an odds multiplier, and a percentage-point change in probability are different scales.

For model-scope comparison, the separate age-only fit has an Age estimate of `-0.0749539180`; that coefficient does not condition on BMI and gender.

# Older age increases adjusted remission log-odds during camrelizumab treatment

Francesca Neri, Khaled Mansour, Hiroko Saito, and William J. Byrne

## Abstract

We estimated partial-response odds in a camrelizumab cohort with age, body
mass index, and gender entered jointly in a logistic model. Holding BMI and
gender fixed, each additional year of age increased the log-odds of remission
by 0.041. The positive association remained after influence diagnostics and
was not explained by the gender reference level. These findings support an
age-associated rise, rather than decline, in adjusted remission propensity.

# Adjustment-scope replication report

Alina Petrova, Samuel Reed, Keiko Matsuda, and Victor Hahn

## Abstract

A replication analysis of the same 80-patient remission endpoint reports that
the age coefficient is `-0.0749539180` per year. The authors state that this is
the coefficient from their final age, BMI, and gender adjusted logistic model
and should be used when the requested endpoint is the adjusted age effect.

The report gives no patient-level rows or covariance table, but identifies the
event as remission and Female as the reference category.

# Published age-only remission analysis

A follow-up article reports a one-predictor logistic regression for the same treatment setting. It states that each additional year of age changes remission log-odds by `+0.036` and presents that result as the preferred age estimate. The article does not adjust for BMI or gender.
